Cross-layer tile decisions

Load a cross-layer study JSON to compare decisions.

Each point pools comparisons at the same layer distance. A missing point means no observations or no skips in the denominator. “Earlier skips still skipped” measures how often reusing a skip agrees with the later layer.

Index matches compare the query with the largest tile-minus-running-max margin and its two winning keys. Replay uses the first recorded layer’s three indices with the current layer’s scores. False skips are measured over fresh keeps, and missed skips over fresh skips.

Row-key replay reuses one key per query row in each tile from the preceding layer. The selected keys’ current scores also supply the running max. The score hit rate counts ties at the exact maximum.

Read the measurements correctly

Score is scaled QKᵀ before softmax; a large absolute negative score is not a large attention weight. Weight is the dense row-normalized softmax on the current recorded trajectory. Margin compares a tile’s row maxima with running row maxima. Masked future positions are excluded. All summaries cover only the selected layers and heads.

Dense recordings support offline threshold exploration. Live sparse recordings contain inputs already changed by earlier skipping. Neither the simulation nor this explorer measures kernel speedup.
